interpretations: Average line UnitPrice is the simple mean of InvoiceLine.UnitPrice per invoice, ignoring Quantity. The overall average is the mean of those per-invoice averages across all invoices.
Average line UnitPrice is weighted by Quantity (sum of UnitPrice×Quantity divided by sum of Quantity) per invoice. The overall average is the mean of the per-invoice values.
The overall average is the mean of all individual invoice lines' UnitPrice, pooled across invoices and not averaged per invoice. Deviation is the invoice average minus this pooled mean.
The overall average is the mean of the invoice averages, but only over invoices that have at least one line. Invoices with no lines are excluded, so their average is null.
Invoices with no lines are kept with a null average unit price, so they appear in the output. Null deviations sort last.
Country is the customer's Country from the Customer table, joined through Invoice.CustomerId.
Country is the invoice's BillingCountry rather than the customer's country.
Deviation is signed (invoice average minus overall average).
Deviation is the absolute value of the difference from the overall average.
The country's average deviation is the mean of the signed deviations of all invoices in that country.
The country's average deviation is the mean of the absolute deviations of invoices in that country.
The country's average deviation is computed over all invoices in the country, including invoices with null averages, which are ignored by AVG.
The final column is the invoice's deviation minus its country's average deviation. This equals the invoice average minus the country's average invoice average when deviations are signed.
"Furthest above" means the largest positive value of deviation minus the country's average deviation, sorted descending.
"Furthest above" means the largest absolute difference from the country's average deviation, in either direction.
"Blanks last" means null values in the sort column come after non-null values in descending order.
Output columns are invoice id, country, average unit price, deviation from the overall average, and deviation minus the country average deviation.
Values are unrounded, with full floating-point precision.
Ties at the 10th position are broken arbitrarily, or by InvoiceId.
Ties at the 10th position are all included, so more than 10 rows may be returned.
Customers with a null Country form their own group, or are excluded from the country comparison.
Some interpretations are missing:
The country's average deviation excludes the invoice itself (leave-one-out mean of the other invoices in that country).
Invoices with no lines are treated as having an average unit price of 0, not null, so they count in the overall and country averages.
Deviation is relative (a percentage or ratio of the overall average) instead of an absolute difference.
Country grouping uses the Customer's Country, but the overall average is taken only over invoices that have a customer country.
The overall average is weighted by Quantity across all lines, pooled (sum of UnitPrice×Quantity over sum of Quantity), instead of an unweighted mean.
The country's average deviation is a pooled average over all invoice lines in the country, not a mean of per-invoice deviations.
"Furthest above" is judged by the country-relative deviation (a ratio or z-score against the country's spread) rather than the raw difference.
queries:
SELECT AVG(avg_price) FROM (SELECT AVG(UnitPrice) AS avg_price FROM InvoiceLine GROUP BY InvoiceId)
SELECT AVG(inv_avg) FROM (SELECT SUM(UnitPrice * Quantity) * 1.0 / SUM(Quantity) AS inv_avg FROM InvoiceLine GROUP BY InvoiceId)
SELECT InvoiceId,
       AVG(UnitPrice) - (SELECT AVG(UnitPrice) FROM InvoiceLine) AS Deviation
FROM InvoiceLine
GROUP BY InvoiceId;
SELECT AVG(inv_avg) AS overall_average
FROM (
  SELECT InvoiceId, AVG(UnitPrice) AS inv_avg
  FROM InvoiceLine
  GROUP BY InvoiceId
);
SELECT i.InvoiceId,
       AVG(il.UnitPrice) AS AvgUnitPrice,
       AVG(il.UnitPrice) - (SELECT AVG(UnitPrice) FROM InvoiceLine) AS Deviation
FROM Invoice i
LEFT JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId
GROUP BY i.InvoiceId
ORDER BY Deviation IS NULL, Deviation;
